questions.enonce_markdown: What are pollutants? Give three examples. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Pollutants** are **substances (chemical, physical or biological agents), usually released into the environment by human activity, in amounts large enough to harm living organisms or to damage the ecosystem or the quality of air, water and soil**. A natural substance (e.g. carbon dioxide, nitrates) becomes a pollutant when its concentration is higher than normal.

**Examples (any three, each with its source and the medium polluted):**

- **Carbon monoxide (CO)** - incomplete combustion of fuel in vehicle engines (air).
- **Sulphur dioxide ($\mathrm{SO_2}$)** - burning of coal and oil in factories (air, acid rain).
- **Nitrates and phosphates** - run-off of fertilisers and detergents from farms and towns (water).
- **Pesticides such as DDT** - sprayed on crops (soil, water, food chains).
- **Heavy metals (lead, mercury)** - industrial effluents and mining, paint and petrol (water, soil).
- **Plastics, oil, domestic sewage and chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)** - dumped waste, oil spills, untreated sewage, aerosols and refrigerators.

questions.enonce_markdown: Describe briefly the hazards of water and air pollution. *[10 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Hazards of water pollution**

- **Sewage and fertiliser (eutrophication):** nitrates and phosphates cause an algal bloom; when the algae die, bacteria decompose them and use up the dissolved oxygen (high **biochemical oxygen demand**), so fish and other aerobic organisms die.
- **Disease:** water contaminated with faeces carries pathogens that cause **cholera, typhoid, dysentery, hepatitis A and bilharzia**.
- **Toxic chemicals:** heavy metals (mercury, lead) and pesticides such as DDT accumulate along the food chain (**bioaccumulation and biomagnification**), causing nerve damage, cancer, thin egg shells in birds and the death of top consumers.
- **Oil spills** coat birds and fish gills and prevent light and oxygen reaching the water; **hot water from factories (thermal pollution)** lowers the oxygen concentration.

**Hazards of air pollution**

- **Carbon monoxide** combines almost irreversibly with haemoglobin to form carboxyhaemoglobin, reducing oxygen transport; it can cause headache, unconsciousness and death.
- **Sulphur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen** cause **bronchitis and asthma** and dissolve in rain to form **acid rain**, which kills trees, acidifies lakes and corrodes buildings.
- **Carbon dioxide and methane** cause the **greenhouse effect** and **global warming** (melting ice, rising sea level, climate change).
- **CFCs** destroy the **ozone layer**, so more ultraviolet radiation reaches the earth: **skin cancer, cataract** and damage to plants and plankton.
- **Smoke and dust particles** cause lung diseases and reduce light for photosynthesis; **lead** from petrol damages the brain of children.

questions.enonce_markdown: Differentiate between biodegradable and non-biodegradable pollutants giving at least one example of each. *[4 marks]* *(6, 10, 4 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| | **Biodegradable pollutants** | **Non-biodegradable pollutants** |
|---|---|---|
| Definition | Pollutants that are **broken down** into harmless simple substances by **decomposers** (bacteria and fungi) and other natural processes | Pollutants that **cannot be broken down** by living organisms, or only extremely slowly |
| Persistence | Short-lived; **do not accumulate** | **Persist and accumulate** in soil, water and living organisms |
| Danger | Harmful only when produced **in excess** (e.g. oxygen depletion by sewage) | Harmful even in **small amounts**; pass along food chains and are **biomagnified** |
| Examples | **Domestic sewage, food waste, paper, wood, animal dung, vegetable waste** | **Plastics, DDT and other persistent pesticides, mercury, lead and other heavy metals, glass, aluminium cans, radioactive waste** |
